summary: We developed a tool which can help farmers and/or professional users to plan ahead what to grow on their field. They can use valid live data from Nasa dataservers, set the needed level of how many data to use, and than the app pulls the data from the databases online, convert every fact to numbers, and create a list which shows a sequence of what is worth producing and why. It also shows the logic behind the calculations so the user can see the full justification. In the pro version the user has the possibility to change the data he/she provided and the data pulled from the databases and see a "what if I change this and that" scenario in the resut list.
details:
Agronauts Application

This application was developed as part of the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Due to time constraints and the size of the team, we were unable to flesh out every detail; consequently, only a demo version has been completed. The application available at the provided link is highly limited in its functionality. It is also important to note that the team members lack extensive expertise in agriculture; therefore, the application may contain shortcomings or logical errors stemming from this limited background.

The core concept is an application designed to assist in the cultivation of a specific area. It provides planning insights by combining historical statistical data, future forecasts, and specific information provided by the user. The final output is a document that—after taking a wide range of factors into account—presents a list of recommendations regarding what the user should cultivate and the appropriate timeframe for doing so. Once the document has been generated and reviewed, the user has several options: they can accept it without reservations and incorporate it into a more comprehensive planning process, or—using the Pro version—they can experiment with the data by creating various scenarios. This allows them to observe how the results shift when input parameters or data retrieved from external databases are modified (for example, a user might possess local, specialized knowledge about weather patterns in their specific area that exceeds the detail found in NASA’s databases; they could therefore override the program’s forecast to reflect higher expected rainfall). Users can also adjust the allocation of their available land—for instance, by dedicating one portion to the top-ranked crop suggested by the list, while testing a different option from the list on the remaining (perhaps smaller) area. Furthermore, users can input potential grant or subsidy information—even if not yet confirmed—to explore how securing such funding might open up new possibilities or alternative recommendations.

Operational logic of the program:

To begin, users must register for the program. During registration, they will need to select their user level. We currently plan for three levels, though this can be expanded based on demand.

Different levels of usage:

·        basic (for very simple "farmers":

o   you can add only a few data: where you are (we can identify his location automatically or ask for the nearest city/(country)+postcode.

o   you can add some plants what you can grow on your field

o   during the calculations we can add some extra plants (we can pull data from NASA public databases what type of soil he has on the given area and what kind of plants can grow on this type of soil

o   during the calculations pull basic data from the databases (weather in the past few years and weather forecast (temperature), rain data, sunny hours, air quality, fire)

o   convert the gathered data into points and finalyze them into a result list. May add some new plants just to give advices

·        medium level (advanced users)

o   you can add more data: what type of plants you cultivated on your field, what kind of fertilizer you used, what kind of plants you have access

o   you can add statistical data from a list what to check on your field (it’s a list of what kind of data are accessible from NASA databases)

o   during the calculations we create a more sophitycated list

o   at the end when we visualyze the result, he has the opportunity to „play” with the result: thick or unthick some of the statistical data to calculate with

·        high level (for specialists)

o   you can click all the possibility accessable from NASA databases to calculate

o   you can add a budget you can use

o   you can add technolgy gadgets you have

o   you can add the reason which is the most important to you int final list

o   you can add a longer period for planning, not just one year, maybe the plan needs longer period to come to

o   you can add other sources you can acquier (fe goverment supply application, regulations what to grow, etc)

you can add the area size and you can split it to mitigate the risk

Once the user has entered their details and selected the desired level of application usage, they can proceed to use the tool. Throughout the process, the user provides the necessary information across various screens and then initiates the generation of a results list. During the calculation phase, the system establishes online connections to relevant NASA databases via APIs, retrieves the required data, performs the necessary computations, and generates a list of recommendations. This list is also saved to the user’s account, allowing them to revisit it at a later time.

Users can also download the generated list, which can serve as the foundation for a comprehensive planting calendar or even a complete restructuring of their approach.
